name: Crypto wallet risk / on-chain monitoring
topic: Beava's current market position - competitor archetypes and market segments beava is positioned in or against, evaluated against the use-case map in ../beava-use-cases/

competitive_landscape.incumbents: Two layers of competition in this segment. (a) The proprietary on-chain-intelligence data graph layer: Chainalysis (Series F Oct 2025, ~$538M total raised, ~$8.6B valuation, ~65% blockchain-analytics market share, >1B addresses mapped, 9 of top-10 CEXes, three acquisitions in the 8 months prior to Oct 2025 including the Alterya fraud-prevention product now monitoring $23B+/month and preventing $300M+ in losses TTM, March 2026 launched blockchain intelligence agents), TRM Labs (unicorn $1B valuation Feb 2026 with $70M Series C led by Blockchain Capital with Goldman + Galaxy + Bessemer + DRW + Citi Ventures, $220M total funding, 150% avg annual revenue growth over 5 years, customers include Circle, Coinbase, Stripe, public sector DOJ/FBI/IRS-CI/HSI, <300ms wallet-screening API), Elliptic ($120M Series D May 2026 led by One Peak with Nasdaq Ventures + Deutsche Bank + British Business Bank, $670M valuation, 2B+ labelled addresses, ~20% blockchain-analytics market share, Lens for transaction monitoring, Holistic sub-second cross-chain, accelerating agentic compliance-analyst roadmap), Merkle Science (Series B Singapore-based, ~$25.6M total raised, $100M Aug-2022 valuation, Compass real-time behaviour-based wallet/transaction monitoring), Crystal Intelligence, Scorechain (250+ institutions, 40+ countries, EU-focused), CipherTrace (now Mastercard, ~10% market share). (b) The streaming / feature-store / KV stacks that exchanges and wallet providers actually use to build their internal velocity-feature layer that joins these third-party risk feeds with their own per-customer behavioural state: Apache Kafka + Apache Flink (the documented dual-pipeline pattern from VeloDB / Apache Doris case studies at a top exchange with 80M+ users - 'Public Chain -> Node Collector -> Go/Rust service -> Redis/Postgres for sub-second; Public Chain -> Kafka -> Flink -> VeloDB for 1-3s deep analytics'), Redis Enterprise / Valkey as the dominant low-latency feature cache, Aerospike for sub-ms feature serving (publicly cited at PayPal/Barclays/TransUnion fraud workloads, analogous deployments in crypto), ClickHouse / VeloDB / Apache Doris / Druid for warm aggregates, Tecton-now-Databricks (Coinbase publicly uses Tecton + Real-Time Mode for fraud feature serving), Feast, Hopsworks, Fennel-now-Databricks, Chalk for ML feature stores. Open-source AML / decision engines: Marble, Jube (AGPLv3). Beava competes most directly with this second layer - the in-house velocity-feature substrate that exchanges stitch from Kafka + Flink + Redis + custom code underneath the third-party risk-label feed.
competitive_landscape.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: Tier-1 blockchain-intelligence data graph (Beava cannot replicate the data moat): Chainalysis (Series F Oct 2025, $8.6B valuation, KYT / Reactor / Storyline / Address Screening, ~45% law-enforcement-user share), TRM Labs ($1B unicorn Feb 2026, Wallet Screening <300ms, BLOCKINT API, 100+ chains, customers Circle/Coinbase/Stripe), Elliptic ($120M Series D May 2026, $670M valuation, Lens + Holistic + Investigator, 2B+ addresses, 2M+ screenings/month), Merkle Science (Compass predictive behavioural monitoring, DMM-postmortem provider), Crystal Intelligence (WazirX-postmortem provider), Scorechain (EU-focused). Crypto-native AML / market surveillance: Solidus Labs HALO (50+ market-abuse typologies, 1T+ events/day, BitMEX integration, 25M+ retail+institutional investors protected, prior $45M Series B + $15M strategic), Nominis, CryptoPolice, AnChain.AI. Travel-Rule providers: Notabene, Sumsub Crypto, 21 Analytics, Veriscope, Shyft. General-purpose fraud / AML platforms with explicit crypto modules: Sardine ($70M Series C Feb 2025, $660M valuation, $145M total raised, 130% ARR growth, Visa partner, explicit crypto-cashout + ATO focus + Avalanche/blockchain integrations), Unit21 (<250ms per-tx, Uphold customer), Hawk.AI (150ms avg, $56M Series C Feb-Apr 2025), Flagright (sub-300ms, MiCA-tactical-playbook publisher), ComplyAdvantage Mesh, Lucinity, Castellum.AI. In-wallet warning providers: Blockaid (MetaMask + Phantom default), Forta, Wallet Guard. MPC custody + policy engine (relevant for use case 23b withdrawal velocity governance): Fireblocks Policy Engine (industry-standard tiered approval / transaction-rule DSL), BitGo, Copper, Liminal (WazirX custody-arrangement provider, itself the subject of the postmortem), Cobo, Coinsdo. Beava slots underneath one of these as the sub-ms velocity-feature substrate; it does NOT replace the chain-intelligence labels, the case manager, the Travel-Rule messaging, the SDN list, the graph engine, or the MPC signing layer.
competitive_landscape.oss_license_posture: Proprietary across every tier-1 incumbent. Chainalysis, TRM Labs, Elliptic, Merkle Science, Crystal, Scorechain, Solidus Labs, Sardine, Unit21, Hawk, Flagright, ComplyAdvantage, Notabene, Fireblocks, BitGo, Copper are all closed-source proprietary SaaS or enterprise software. There is no Apache-2.0 / BSL / 'rug-pulled' incumbent in the crypto wallet-risk segment at all - the closed-loop ML + proprietary-on-chain-cluster-labelling business model is structurally hostile to open source. The only OSS-adjacent players are the generic AML engines (Marble, Jube AGPLv3) which do not provide on-chain risk labels. Beava's Apache-2.0 posture (no open-core split, no acquisition risk, license-clean for embedding inside a third-party regtech vendor's product) is a real wedge for two specific buyers: (1) the exchange's in-house risk-engineering team building the velocity-feature substrate underneath a TRM/Chainalysis feed, and (2) the wallet provider or DeFi protocol that resists SaaS lock-in. It is NOT a wedge for the primary compliance buyer (MLRO / CCO) who is procuring a turnkey on-chain intelligence platform.
competitive_landscape.hyperscaler_bundling_threat: Medium. Unlike payments fraud where Stripe Radar collapses the fraud-team's job into the PSP subscription, there is no equivalent 'hyperscaler bundles a good-enough on-chain risk scorer into a subscription you already pay for' dynamic in crypto - the on-chain data moat sits with the three independent specialists (Chainalysis, TRM Labs, Elliptic), and the hyperscalers (AWS, GCP, Azure) do not own that graph. The bundling pressure shows up differently: (a) Databricks-after-Tecton-and-Fennel can offer a 'good-enough' real-time feature substrate to any crypto buyer already on Databricks - especially Coinbase, which publicly uses Tecton + Spark Real-Time Mode; (b) Confluent managed Kafka + Flink ships a credible OSS alternative to the in-house Kafka+Flink stack that beava collapses; (c) Redis-Cloud and Valkey (Ubuntu 26.04 default) offer the velocity-counter cache layer for nearly free; (d) the third-party risk vendors themselves (Chainalysis, TRM, Elliptic) are quietly extending into agentic compliance and case management (Chainalysis intelligence agents March 2026, Elliptic accelerating agentic roadmap May 2026), which compresses the buyer's perceived 'need for our own velocity layer' if the vendor ships sufficient API depth. The threat is real but indirect, and the segment is structurally winnable for a single-binary OSS challenger that targets the in-house feature substrate beneath the third-party label feed.
competitive_landscape.integration_surface: Heterogeneous and split between on-chain firehoses and exchange-internal event buses. Upstream producers: Ethereum / L2 archive nodes via JSON-RPC (geth, erigon, nethermind, reth), Bitcoin Core RPC, Solana RPC (Helius, Triton), node-as-a-service providers (Alchemy, QuickNode, Infura, Helius, Bitquery, Blockdaemon, GetBlock), indexers (The Graph, Goldsky, SubQuery, Substreams, Bitquery, Allium, Dune, Footprint), chain-specific firehoses (Solana Yellowstone gRPC, Ethereum Geyser-style); plus exchange-internal Kafka/Kinesis tx-firehose + withdrawal-orchestrator HTTP/REST handlers. Third-party risk-label inbound: Chainalysis KYT webhook, TRM Labs BLOCKINT API + webhook, Elliptic Holistic API, Merkle Science, Crystal, Scorechain. Sanctions: OFAC SDN list (CSV/JSON, daily), EU consolidated, UK OFSI, UN. Off-chain: KYC service (Sumsub/Persona/Onfido/Jumio), MPC platform webhooks (Fireblocks/BitGo/Copper/Cobo). Beava's HTTP/JSON :8080 + framed-TCP :8081 (JSON/msgpack) push-on-event model is a clean fit for (a) the in-house withdrawal-orchestrator that already makes a synchronous risk-engine call before signing the on-chain tx, and (b) the wallet provider's signing-modal lookup, and (c) a thin 'node firehose -> beava TCP' sidecar pattern. It is friction for the Kafka-first feature-store pattern (Tecton/Feast/Hopsworks/Fennel) that the documented top-exchange stack assumes - a Kafka source connector or sidecar is needed, not in v0. gRPC support would close a recognised gap with Tecton/Chalk and matches what CEXes standardise on internally.
competitive_landscape.scoring_engine_coupling: Both, plus a third stage for use case 23b. Crypto risk stacks always run rules-and-ML in parallel: rule engines (vendor DSLs inside TRM/Chainalysis/Elliptic, no-code engines in Unit21/Sardine/Hawk/Flagright, Drools/OpenRules/FEEL in custom builds, Fireblocks Policy DSL on the custody side) on top of features, and ML scorers (XGBoost/LightGBM/ONNX/isolation-forest classifiers, GNN-based illicit-cluster detectors as published on the Elliptic dataset, increasingly transformer-based sequence models per Coinbase publications). Withdrawal-velocity governance (use case 23b) adds a third stage - a tiered-approval workflow engine (auto / single-approver / quorum / freeze). Beava is feature-serving only; the buyer plugs it into all three stages, and the missing trigger / 'fire-when-counter-crosses-threshold' webhook surface is what blocks beava from also driving the response loop directly.

beava_position_lens.beava_credible_wedge: Eight concrete reasons a buyer in this segment - specifically the in-house risk-engineering team at a CEX, wallet provider, or DeFi protocol building the velocity-feature substrate underneath a TRM / Chainalysis / Elliptic data feed - would pick beava over the Kafka+Flink+Redis+custom-code alternative: (1) Single binary, Apache-2.0, no broker / no ETL, no open-core rug-pull risk - license-clean for embedding inside a third-party regtech vendor's product (Notabene / Sumsub / 21 Analytics / Veriscope can ship beava as the feature substrate without IP entanglement), and procurement-clean for an exchange MLRO who wants 'no SaaS lock-in on the security-critical path'. (2) Declarative @bv.event / @bv.table primitives express per-(address, chain_id) and per-(account_id, coin) velocity counters, mixer-interaction recency, peer-group z-score, fan-in/fan-out, drain-burst as schema rather than Flink jobs + Lua scripts - this is the exact layer that the documented top-exchange Kafka+Flink+VeloDB stack hand-codes today. (3) ~684k EPS on a single Apple-M4 core (TCP+msgpack, parallel=16) is comfortably above any single-tenant CEX or wallet-provider steady-state and survives Bybit-class drain bursts (14,600 signed transactions in minutes); leaves ample headroom for 30-150 feature reads per decision. (4) Sub-ms TCP batch_get is well inside any wallet-warning (<200ms), exchange-withdrawal hold (<300ms), DEX-pre-trade, or signing-modal budget by an order of magnitude - inside TRM's published <300ms wallet-screening SLA and Elliptic's sub-second Holistic. (5) Atomic per-event update-and-read - 'this withdrawal_request must update the (account, coin) sum_5m before being threshold-checked' - is a class of bug that has bitten production Redis+Lua deployments in concurrent-burst conditions and is exactly what beava's @bv.event model is designed to prevent. (6) HTTP/JSON + framed-TCP (JSON or msgpack) lets a Rust/Go node firehose, a Python compliance scorer, a TypeScript wallet-warning UI, and a Java rules engine all call beava directly without a Kafka broker hop. (7) WAL + periodic snapshot + refuse-on-network-FS is the right default for an exchange operator who would otherwise quietly run on EFS and break crash recovery. (8) ~60 first-class aggregation primitives covering counters, velocities, distances, distinct-cardinality (HLL), heavy-hitter (CMS), and quantile (t-digest/KLL) sketches map directly onto the documented feature catalogue: hop-distance cache (cached as key-value), inbound/outbound velocity per window, distinct-counterparty HLL, top-1-counterparty-share-of-amount, t-digest amount quantile per address, days-since-address-first-seen. Net: beava cannot replicate Chainalysis/TRM/Elliptic's proprietary on-chain data graph (that data moat is unassailable on a 12-month horizon), and would be foolish to try. The credible wedge is to BE the in-platform velocity-feature substrate that joins the third-party label feed with the exchange's own per-customer behavioural state - the layer that today is Kafka+Flink+Redis+custom code.
beava_position_lens.beava_disqualifiers: Fifteen concrete gaps blocking production deployment in this segment, derived from use cases 23 and 23b's open_engineering_gaps and SOURCE-OF-TRUTH.md v0 invariants (roughly decreasing priority): (1) No TLS on :8080/:8081/:8090 in v0 - disqualifying for any regulated VASP, even on a private subnet; security teams want mTLS to the feature store given the 2024-2025 attack surface. (2) No authn/authz / RBAC / per-tenant namespaces - every regulated buyer needs per-tenant tokens, per-role access, per-team audit; the risk-vendor multi-tenant embed case requires it doubly. (3) No trigger / 'fire-when-counter-crosses-threshold' webhook - withdrawal-velocity governance and wallet-warning emission are fundamentally event-driven ('freeze account when sum_5m > k', 'route to quorum when z-score > 4', 'pause withdrawals when min_hop_to_OFAC <= 1'); this is the single highest-leverage feature add for the segment per both use case files. (4) No in-process sharding / no horizontal-scale story - caps single-tenant scale at one node; address-grain cardinality (100M-1B+) and (account, counterparty_address) pair-grain are the hardest single-node-RAM limits in beava's whole use-case map. (5) No hot-standby / synchronous-WAL replication - losing 90-365d behavioural baselines on a crash is unacceptable to MLROs and risk-engineering teams. (6) In-memory only with no tiered storage (RAM -> NVMe) - top-tier-exchange address-grain working set (200 GB - 8 TB at 2-8 KB/address) exceeds single-node RAM. (7) No native point-in-time / as-of read - regulators under MiCA / FATF / FinCEN explicitly expect reproducibility of decision-time feature values ('what was min_hop_to_OFAC for address X at 14:32:07Z on 2026-02-14?'). (8) No re-org / tombstone / compensating-write semantics for chain reorganisations - a correctness-critical gap unique to this domain (Ethereum 1-2 block reorgs, Bitcoin 6-block, mempool-then-confirmed double-publish, node-provider reconnect replay). (9) No native on-chain risk-label integration hook (OFAC SDN, mixer lists, scam DB, Chainalysis/TRM/Elliptic webhook) - every competitor ships this. (10) No native graph / hop-distance primitive - the hop-to-OFAC-or-mixer feature, which is the most-asked feature in this domain, requires offline graph computation cached as a key-value lookup; beava has no graph layer. (11) No native idempotency keys on push (dedupe by (tx_hash, log_index, chain_id) or end_to_end_id) - required for at-least-once node firehoses to avoid double-counting velocity and Travel-Rule aggregates. (12) No multi-tenancy - wallet-provider and regtech-vendor SaaS embedding needs per-tenant namespaces. (13) No data-residency controls (EU-only RAM, US-only RAM, JP-only RAM) - MiCA / EU TFR / GDPR / JFSA / NYDFS push EU-customer data on-EU. (14) No Kafka source / sink connector - every CEX has Kafka or Kinesis in front of the risk pipeline. (15) No case-management UI / no SAR-narrative generator / no Travel-Rule messaging / no closed-loop network effect - beava is feature-substrate only and never owns the compliance product itself. Also missing: per-read audit log (regulator-required for MiCA / FATF reproducibility), gRPC surface, deterministic-replay-with-hash from WAL, GDPR right-to-erasure compatible with aggregate counters, Prometheus / OpenTelemetry exporters.
beava_position_lens.time_to_credible_offering: 6-12mo for the design-partner shape (one mid-tier CEX or wallet provider's in-house risk-engineering team using beava as the velocity-feature substrate underneath their TRM/Chainalysis feed), 12mo+ for production-grade at a tier-1 CEX or regulated EU CASP. Breakdown: the first-tier procurement-non-starter gaps (TLS+auth+RBAC, per-tenant namespaces, audit log, items 1-2 above) are roughly 2-3 months. The single-highest-leverage gap (trigger / webhook surface, item 3) is another 1-2 months given how it touches the existing @bv.table primitive. The MiCA / FATF audit-reproducibility gaps (point-in-time/as-of reads item 7, deterministic-replay-with-hash, per-read audit log) are 2-3 months. The chain-correctness gaps (re-org/tombstone item 8, idempotency tokens item 11) are 1-2 months but novel-design-territory. The integration gaps (on-chain risk-label hook item 9, graph/hop-distance primitive item 10, Kafka connector item 14, on-chain firehose adapter library) are 2-3 months. The tier-1-scale gaps (in-process sharding item 4, hot-standby/replication item 5, tiered storage item 6, multi-tenancy item 12, data-residency item 13) are 6+ months and are blockers only for top-tier exchanges - not required for the first design partners (a mid-tier exchange or wallet provider fits inside the single-node envelope). Pre-sales activity (build a public onchain_risk demo at examples/onchain_risk that ingests a streamed mempool + confirmed-tx feed, computes velocity + mixer-flag + hop-distance features at (address, chain_id) grain against the public Elliptic Bitcoin dataset + Etherscan API + OFAC SDN list) is a 2-4 week sprint and unblocks the first credible buyer conversation.

evidence_and_verdict.validation_signals_today: Zero public beava signals in this segment, strong indirect validation that the segment shape and buyer pain are real. Beava-side: no publicly named crypto / web3 user, no published case study, no conference talk, no crypto-vertical demo in the repo (existing python/beava/demos/ contains adtech, ecommerce, fraud - but no onchain_risk, no crypto-exchange-withdrawal, no wallet-screening). No beava-specific Discord / GitHub Discussion / RFC thread on crypto wallet risk was located. Competitor-side validation that the segment is large, regulator-pulled, and structurally needs the velocity-feature substrate beava could provide: (a) TRM Labs $1B unicorn Feb 2026 with $70M Series C and 150% avg ARR growth over 5 years; Chainalysis $8.6B valuation Series F Oct 2025 with 65% market share; Elliptic $120M Series D May 2026 at $670M valuation; Sardine $70M Series C Feb 2025 at $660M with 130% ARR growth and explicit crypto-cashout focus; Hawk.AI $56M Series C 2025 - this segment is well-funded and procurement-mature. (b) Documented in-house stack at a top crypto exchange (80M+ users) using Kafka + Flink + VeloDB + Redis + custom service code for exactly the velocity-feature layer beava collapses (VeloDB / Apache Doris case study). (c) Binance public material on streaming pipelines + Flink + Kafka feature stores for fraud detection (Binance Square 'A Feature Engineering Case Study in Consistency and Fraud Detection'). (d) Coinbase publicly uses Tecton + Databricks Real-Time Mode for fraud feature serving - the exact substrate beava would replace. (e) Headline incidents validating the urgency: Bybit $1.5B Lazarus hack Feb 2025, WazirX ~$235M Jul 2024, DMM ~$305M May 2024, OKX $504M FinCEN penalty Feb 2025, Paxful $3.5M FinCEN penalty Dec 2025; Chainalysis $3.4B stolen in crypto in 2025 ($2.2B in 2024), DPRK/Lazarus $2.02B in 2025 alone. (f) MiCA full applicability transitional sunset July 1 2026 + EU TFR no-de-minimis from Dec 30 2024 + FATF June 2025 update flagging persistent Travel Rule implementation gaps = every EU CASP is in build mode right now on transaction monitoring + withdrawal-side surveillance. (g) ESMA 2025 guidelines explicitly highlight 'rapid exit after cash-out' withdrawal-velocity pattern as a red-flag pattern requiring on-chain + off-chain surveillance. Beava knows who the buyer is (in-house risk-engineering team at a CEX, wallet provider, DeFi protocol, or embedded inside a regtech vendor) but has zero published proof points to that buyer.
evidence_and_verdict.verdict: Compete - the in-platform velocity-feature substrate wedge is real and structurally winnable (Apache-2.0 license posture clean for embedding, single-binary collapses the documented Kafka+Flink+Redis stack, sub-ms batch_get inside every published vendor SLA, ~60 primitives map directly onto the documented feature catalogue, ~684k EPS survives Bybit-class drain bursts), but the segment is data-moat-defended (Chainalysis $8.6B / 1B addresses, TRM Labs $1B unicorn / 100+ chains, Elliptic $670M / 2B addresses) and beava must explicitly pitch as the layer UNDERNEATH those feeds, not as a replacement. 6-12 months of focused engineering on (TLS + auth + RBAC + per-tenant namespaces), the trigger/webhook surface (highest-leverage single add), idempotency tokens on push, re-org/tombstone semantics, audit log + point-in-time reads, and a published 'beava + Chainalysis KYT webhook + XGBoost in 200ms' notebook against the canonical Elliptic Bitcoin dataset + OFAC SDN list + synthetic mempool feed are required before the first design-partner conversation. Do NOT pitch this as a Chainalysis / TRM / Elliptic replacement - that is a different sale, with a different buyer (MLRO / CCO procuring a turnkey on-chain intelligence platform with a 1B+-address graph), and a data network beava cannot match. Pitch it as the open-source single-binary feature substrate that an exchange's in-house risk-engineering team uses to compute per-customer per-address per-coin velocity, drain-burst, mixer-recency, hop-distance-cached, and z-score-vs-envelope features in sub-ms, joining the third-party risk-label feed with the platform's own behavioural state. The regulatory pull (MiCA Jul 2026 transitional sunset, EU TFR no-de-minimis, FATF 99-jurisdiction Travel Rule, OKX/Paxful enforcement, Bybit/WazirX/DMM/Indodax/CoinDCX postmortems) is structural and accelerating; this is not a 'watch' segment.
